correctness.rationale: PASS: The frozen RESULT.md constructs H^2=⊕_{n≥0} B^n K_B for the finite inner Blaschke multiplier and shows d distinct normalized evaluation kernels span K_B by the positive Cauchy determinant. Thus all infinite-orbit Riesz bounds reduce to the finite seed Gram. Expanding the Cauchy double alternant yields log det=Σ_{k=1}^{d-1}Σ_j L_r(θ_{j+k}-θ_j), L_r(t)=log[2r sin(t/2)/|1-r²e^{it}|]. Differentiation gives -L_r''≥c_r=(1-r²)²/(4(1+r²)²); strong Jensen and the exact cyclic identity Σ_{k,j}(ε_{j+k}-ε_j)²=2d Σ_j(ε_j-mean ε)² give the claimed quadratic loss, with equality only for rotated regular polygons. For d=2, the second-order near-antipodal loss tends to c_r h², proving uniform optimality. Fourier diagonalization gives λ_l=d(1-r²)r^{2l}/(1-r^{2d}) and uniform two-sided frame bounds iff sup_d d(1-r_d)<∞. I independently evaluated the d=2 quadratic coefficient at r=0.2,0.5,0.8 and h=0.02,0.01; all ratios tend to the displayed c_r. Script trials alone are not the proof.
